Playbook.name: Windows — Elastic Agent Service Terminated - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A process (net/sc/wmic/powershell/taskkill/PsKill/ProcessHacker) stopped or killed the Elastic Agent service. Triage question: is an attacker disabling monitoring, or is this a legitimate agent maintenance/upgrade?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Killing the Elastic Agent blinds detection on the host - a defense-evasion step before or during an intrusion.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Agent terminated
Signal.Details: stop/kill of the Elastic Agent service by net/sc/wmic/taskkill/etc.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the agent was terminated.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the Elastic Agent termination is defense evasion or legitimate maintenance.

Step.name: What stopped the agent and how
Step.Purpose: The killing process/command and account reveal maintenance vs tampering.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(net|net1|sc|wmic|powershell|pwsh|taskkill|pskill|processhacker).*" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE cl LIKE "*elastic*agent*" OR cl LIKE "*elastic-agent*" OR cl LIKE "*elasticendpoint*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: taskkill/PsKill/ProcessHacker against the agent by a non-admin = tampering. sc stop by an admin during a documented upgrade window is maintenance. Note whether other defenses were touched too.

Step.name: What happened on the host after the agent stopped
Step.Purpose: Activity right after the agent stops is what the attacker wanted unmonitored (note: agent-off means Sysmon may still log).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4688","4624","7045","4697") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Security-channel events still flow even if the agent's endpoint component is killed; suspicious activity here after the kill supports tampering.

Node.Condition: The agent was killed via taskkill/PsKill/ProcessHacker by a non-admin, or amid other suspicious activity.
Node.Result: True Positive (Defense Evasion - IR, restore monitoring)

Node.Condition: A documented agent upgrade/maintenance by an admin under a window.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-AGENT-KILL, INV-02-AGENT-AFTER to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the maintenance; close as false_positive.
Restore the agent; isolate the host; open IR.
Reconstruct the unmonitored window from the Security channel.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A management tool restarting the agent unexpectedly.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
